Reproduction command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-i1M8e9/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-i1M8e9/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-i1M8e9/claude-501 bun -e 'import { mkdtempSync, rmSync } from "node:fs"; import { tmpdir } from "node:os"; import { join } from "node:path"; import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process"; import { recordLegacyWorktree } from "./src/git/legacy.ts
findings.failure_scenario: A migration-eligible local run resumes with a missing sidecar and a linked worktree attached to repo.localPath/.git rather than the factory cache. Resume fails despite intact administration and retained commits.

findings.title: Main-red suppression never resumes for an unchanged PR
findings.detail: The classifier returns true after suppressing a failure because main is red, so the poller clears ciPending. Subsequent unchanged PR observations do not inspect main. Main can recover while the PR remains permanently suppressed, with neither a rerun nor ci.needs_fix. Targeted command: `bun test /private/tmp/lr-yRua1O/claude-501/ci-review.test.ts`. The recovery-retention assertion failed: `Expected: false; Received: true`.
findings.failure_scenario: Main and a factory PR fail the same check. Initial classification suppresses the PR. Main subsequently passes, but the PR's failed check and SHA remain unchanged across every poll.

findings.title: An accepted rerun with a lost response cannot become flake evidence
findings.detail: A rerun claim is persisted as rerun_requested before the POST, but reconciliation examines only rerunning rows. If GitHub accepts the POST and the response is lost—or the daemon stops before finishCiFailure—the later same-SHA pass is ignored. If the original failure is still visible, line 352 instead marks the claim failed_again without inspecting the new attempt. Targeted command: `bun test /private/tmp/lr-yRua1O/claude-501/ci-review.test.ts`. Output: `Expected: "failed_then_passed"; Received: "rerun_requested"`.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub starts attempt 2, the rerun POST response fails in transit, and attempt 2 passes at the original SHA. The ledger retains rerun_requested instead of recording the flake.

findings.title: Security tests can be rerun when their names occur after the first error line
findings.detail: The security guard examines only the check name, job name, and one selected signature line. It ignores security test names elsewhere in the log, although transient detection scans the entire log. A generic test job can therefore rerun security tests and record them in the flake ledger, violating the explicit exclusion. Targeted command: `bun test /private/tmp/lr-yRua1O/claude-501/ci-review.test.ts`. Output for the security fixture: `Expected: 0; Received: 1` rerun POST.
findings.failure_scenario: A job named test logs `error: test suite failed`, followed by `FAIL security/authorization.test.ts` and `Test timed out after 1000ms`. The signature selects the generic first line, unsafe is false, and the job is rerun.

findings.title: Resume suppressed PR failures when main recovers
findings.detail: A main-red inspection clears ciPending. Subsequent unchanged PR observations never inspect main again, so its recovery cannot resume the suppressed rerun or needs-fix reaction. Command: bun test /private/tmp/lr-UWn1Tq/claude-501/ci-review.test.js. Output: After main recovery: {"reruns":0,"pending":false,"mainState":{"test":{"red":true,"episode":1}}}; assertion failed: Expected length: 1, Received length: 0.
findings.failure_scenario: PR and main both fail the test check. Main subsequently passes, while the PR SHA and failed check remain unchanged. The PR remains suppressed indefinitely.

findings.title: Reconcile reruns whose POST response was lost
findings.detail: Only rerunning rows are reconciled. A successful POST with a lost response, or a crash before finishCiFailure, leaves rerun_requested. A later same-SHA success is ignored; another failure can prematurely mark the request failed_again without checking its actual attempt. Command: bun test /private/tmp/lr-UWn1Tq/claude-501/ci-review.test.js. Output: After same-SHA pass: rerun_requested; assertion failed: Expected: "failed_then_passed", Received: "rerun_requested".
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts the rerun, the connection resets before its response arrives, and attempt 2 passes at the original SHA. The ledger never records the flake.

findings.title: Resolve completed reruns with skipped conclusions
findings.detail: Completed conclusions outside success and bad fall through without changing rerunning. A skipped rerun therefore keeps successful CI pending forever and causes repeated REST inspection. Command: bun test /private/tmp/lr-UWn1Tq/claude-501/ci-review.test.js. Output: After completed skipped rerun: {"completed":false,"outcome":"rerunning"}; assertion failed: Expected: true, Received: false.
findings.failure_scenario: A timed-out job is rerun, but an attempt-dependent condition skips it on attempt 2. GitHub reports the job completed/skipped and the rollup SUCCESS; the ledger remains rerunning indefinitely.

gold.summary: A definitively refused CI rerun remains pending indefinitely.

findings.title: Rejected rerun requests remain pending indefinitely
findings.detail: The rerun is claimed before the POST, but a definitive rejection leaves its outcome as rerun_requested. Subsequent inspections wait for a higher workflow attempt and suppress ci.needs_fix, although no rerun was created. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". The rejected-request test failed with "Expected: 1\nReceived: 0" for the needs-fix item count after three subsequent inspections.
findings.failure_scenario: A timed-out job's rerun POST returns HTTP 403. The workflow remains at attempt 1; every subsequent poll leaves the ledger at rerun_requested and emits no ci.needs_fix.

findings.title: A later sibling-only attempt hides the originating rerun
findings.detail: Reconciliation searches only the workflow's latest attempt. Selective job reruns can create a later attempt containing another job, so the originating job's completed rerun exists only in an earlier attempt. The classifier then throws on every inspection rather than recording its result. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". The fixture supplied a successful originating job in attempt 2 and another job in attempt 3; output was "error: Ambiguous CI rerun job".
findings.failure_scenario: The factory reruns job A in attempt 2, where it succeeds. Before the next poll, someone reruns sibling job B, creating attempt 3 containing only B. Job A remains rerunning indefinitely despite available successful evidence at the same SHA.

findings.title: A rejected rerun request leaves the failure pending forever
findings.detail: The claim persists rerun_requested before the POST, but an explicit rejection only throws. Subsequent inspections wait for a later workflow attempt that will never exist and suppress ci.needs_fix. Direct check `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` produced `Rejected rerun after four polls: {"posts":1,"outcome":"rerun_requested","feed":0}` and `ASSERTION FAILURE: rejected rerun should emit needs_fix` (`0 !== 1`).
findings.failure_scenario: A timed-out job is eligible for rerun, but GitHub returns HTTP 422 without starting another attempt. Every later poll retains rerun_requested and emits no actionable result.

findings.title: Completed skipped or neutral reruns never resolve
findings.detail: Reconciliation handles success and conclusions in bad, then continues for all other conclusions—even completed jobs. A skipped or neutral rerun remains rerunning permanently, and a SUCCESS rollup repeatedly returns false. Direct check `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` produced `Skipped rerun: {"done":false,"outcome":"rerunning","feed":0}` and `ASSERTION FAILURE: completed skipped rerun must resolve pending inspection` (`false !== true`).
findings.failure_scenario: A failed job is rerun, but its job condition excludes subsequent attempts, so attempt 2 completes as skipped and the rollup becomes SUCCESS. The original ledger row remains rerunning and REST inspection continues indefinitely across restarts.

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: Playwright security failures can be automatically rerun
findings.detail: Security detection ignores Playwright failure headings such as `1) [chromium] › tests/security.spec.ts:10:1 › rejects unauthorized access`. In a generic job concluded timed_out, that evidence does not prevent recording the failure and rerunning the job. This violates the security-test exclusion. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probes.ts"` produced `observed rerun POSTs: 1 ledger rows: 1` and `FAIL Playwright security timeout never reruns ... 1 !== 0`.
findings.failure_scenario: A generic test job times out and its log contains a Playwright failure heading naming security.spec.ts; the step name is generic and there are no failure annotations.

findings.title: Indented Playwright timeout diagnostics are not classified as transient
findings.detail: The Playwright alternative is anchored without allowing leading whitespace. Standard reporter output such as `    Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.` therefore produces ci.needs_fix instead of a rerun. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probes.ts"` produced `observed rerun POSTs: 0 needs_fix items: 1` and `FAIL indented Playwright timeout is transient ... 0 !== 1`.
findings.failure_scenario: A GitHub Actions job concludes failure after a Playwright test timeout, with the timeout diagnostic indented in its downloaded log.

findings.title: Main-red alerts are deduplicated per check instead of per repository
findings.detail: Each failing check name receives a separate ci.main_red key. When test and lint fail on both main and a PR, two repository items are emitted, contrary to the requested single repository item. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probes.ts"` produced `observed ci.main_red items: 2` and `FAIL one main-red feed item per repository ... 2 !== 1`.
findings.failure_scenario: One repository has two checks failing on main and the same two checks failing on a factory PR.

findings.title: Main-red failures are omitted from the failure ledger
findings.detail: The main-red branch continues before job inspection and recordCiFailure, so these PR failure signatures, SHAs, runner images, and outcomes are never persisted. Pausing reactions should not discard the requested failure history. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probes.ts"` produced `observed main-red ledger rows: 0` and `FAIL main-red PR failures enter the ledger ... 0 !== 1`.
findings.failure_scenario: A non-security check fails on both main and a factory PR; the PR closes before main recovers, leaving no ledger record of its failure.

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: A rejected rate-limited rerun stays pending indefinitely
findings.detail: The rerun is claimed before POST, but HTTP 429 leaves its outcome as rerun_requested. Subsequent inspections wait for a higher workflow attempt that will never exist because GitHub rejected the request, while suppressing ci.needs_fix. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-sHSr7q/claude-501/ci-review/probe.ts rate`. Output included `429 subsequent inspection complete: false` on three inspections, `429 final: {"outcomes":["rerun_requested"],"needsFix":0,"rerunPosts":1}`, and `ASSERTION FAILED: a definitively rate-limited POST remains pending forever with no ci.needs_fix`.
findings.failure_scenario: A transient job is eligible for rerun, but GitHub responds with HTTP 429. No rerun starts, and every later inspection retains the pending claim across restarts without emitting an actionable result.

findings.title: Reconciliation loses results when a later attempt reruns another job
findings.detail: Reconciliation reads only the workflow's latest attempt. Partial job reruns can leave the originating job's completed result in an earlier attempt while the latest attempt contains another job. The missing name is then treated as ambiguous forever, preventing flake recording and further classification. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-sHSr7q/claude-501/ci-review/probe.ts latest`. With the original job succeeding in attempt 2 and another job succeeding in attempt 3, output was `Later unrelated attempt: Ambiguous CI rerun job outcome: rerunning` and `ASSERTION FAILED: a successful rerun in attempt 2 is never read after an unrelated attempt 3`.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory reruns job A from attempt 1; A succeeds in attempt 2. Before the next inspection, another job is rerun in attempt 3. GitHub reports run_attempt=3, whose jobs omit A, leaving A's ledger outcome permanently rerunning despite its successful same-SHA rerun.

gold.summary: Catalog mutation can invalidate a shadowed retained policy and prevent the daemon from restarting.

findings.title: An older probe can overwrite discovery after provider re-enablement
findings.detail: Probe results have no generation or ordering guard. Disabling and re-enabling a provider starts another probe, but the previous probe can finish afterward and replace the newer served list in memory and SQLite. Reproduction command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-MqlmDM/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-MqlmDM/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-MqlmDM/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-MqlmDM/claude-501/discovery-order.ts. Output: `After new probe: [ "new-build" ]`; `After stale probe finishes: [ "old-build" ]`; `AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly deep-equal`, actual `["old-build"]`, expected `["new-build"]`.
findings.failure_scenario: A probe receives headers for old-build but its body is delayed. The operator disables and re-enables the provider after replacing its model. The new probe records new-build, then the older body completes. Routing subsequently skips new-build and permits the obsolete build until another probe succeed

findings.title: Deletion can leave a persisted policy that prevents daemon restart
findings.detail: Deletion checks only operator routing rows. A runtime model can also be referenced by the file policy, which Factory loads after restoring runtime models. DELETE succeeds for that reference, but the next startup fails in readPolicy because the model is now missing. Reproduction command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-MqlmDM/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-MqlmDM/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-MqlmDM/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-MqlmDM/claude-501/catalog-delete-reload.ts. Output: `DELETE succeeded; runtime rows: 0`, followed by `AssertionError: Got unwanted exception` and `Invalid routing policy routing/policy.json` with `unknown model ID "codex/experiment"`.
findings.failure_scenario: Add codex/experiment, reference it in routing/policy.json, and restart successfully. With no operator cell referencing it, delete the model through the catalog API. The next daemon restart aborts while loading the unchanged policy file.

gold.summary: Catalog mutation can invalidate a shadowed retained policy and prevent the daemon from restarting.

findings.title: Deleting a model referenced by the file-backed policy prevents restart
findings.detail: remove() checks only persisted operator cells. The evals policy loaded from routing/policy.json can also reference runtime models, but deletion leaves those references intact. Factory subsequently calls readPolicy() against the reduced catalog during startup, which throws and prevents the daemon from starting. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {RuntimeCatalog} from "./src/router/runtime-catalog.ts"; import {validatePolicy} from "./src/router/policy.ts"; const models=[{id:"codex/experiment",provider:"codex",source:"runtime",supportedEfforts:[]}]; const policy={triage:{default:["codex/experiment"]}}; const store={routingCells:()=>[],writeRuntimeModel:()=>{},publishCatalog:()=>{}}; const cat
findings.failure_scenario: Add codex/experiment, write an evals policy cell naming it, restart to activate that policy, then delete the model when no operator cell references it. Deletion succeeds, routing loses the target, and the next daemon restart fails while loading routing/policy.json.

gold.summary: Effort removal is persisted without checking policy cells hidden by operator overrides.

findings.title: An older probe can overwrite newer discovery results
findings.detail: Probe results are applied without checking their generation. Enabling a provider starts another probe while an earlier request can remain in flight. The older response can overwrite the newer served set and incorrectly exclude available models. Reproduced with `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-fW7W4l/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-fW7W4l/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-fW7W4l/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-fW7W4l/claude-501/catalog-review.ts`. Output: `new probe: [ "mtplx-qwen38-27b-optimized-quality" ]`, then `after old probe: [ "retired-backend" ]`; the route returned no candidates and `reason: "not served by mtplx"`.
findings.failure_scenario: A probe starts before a backend replacement. Disable and re-enable the provider, then let the new probe finish before the old one. The old model list wins and routing skips the currently served model until another successful probe.

findings.title: PATCH cannot clear an optional default effort
findings.detail: Omitting effort preserves the old value, while supplying null fails modelSchema validation. JSON cannot transmit undefined, so the API offers no way to remove a default effort. This matters for Claude-backed agent roles, where an unset effort is required. The same isolated command produced `clear effort: Error: model.effort: invalid or missing field` for PATCH `{effort:null}`.
findings.failure_scenario: Add a runtime model with effort `none`, then try to remove that default so its bare ID can serve an agent role. PATCH cannot perform the change; the operator must delete and recreate the model, first clearing any blocking policy cells.

gold.summary: Effort removal is persisted without checking policy cells hidden by operator overrides.

findings.title: Deletion can invalidate the startup routing policy
findings.detail: Deletion checks only stored operator cells. An evals policy loaded at startup can also reference a runtime model, so deletion succeeds while leaving that policy invalid. The next startup rejects the policy and prevents the daemon from starting. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-catalog-boundaries.ts" delete. Output: DELETE succeeded; restart rejects policy: unknown model ID "codex/experiment", followed by a ZodError for triage.default[0].
findings.failure_scenario: Add codex/experiment, reference it in the evals policy's triage.default cell, restart to load that policy, and delete the model while no operator cell references it. The next restart fails policy validation.

findings.title: An older probe can overwrite newer discovery results
findings.detail: The enabled check occurs before awaiting the response body, and probe results have no generation guard. A response still being parsed can complete after disable/re-enable and a newer successful probe, replacing the current served list with stale IDs. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-catalog-boundaries.ts" probe. Output: served after old response: ["old-build"]; AssertionError with actual ["old-build"] and expected ["new-build"].
findings.failure_scenario: A probe receives headers for old-build but delays its body. Disable and re-enable the provider, then complete a newer probe serving new-build. Completing the older body overwrites discovery, causing the router to skip new-build and potentially invoke the retired build.

Routing previews remain stale after quota or cooldown expiry without an event.
Clearing a default effort omits the field from PATCH and leaves the old value stored.
Catalog history disappears on reload and does not include changes made by another client.

findings.title: Prefill retry chains using each role's actual routing complexity
findings.detail: The picker applies the original run's complexity to every role and submits those chains as explicit overrides. However, pipeline triage always routes with small, and deep-profile review routes with large. Opening this picker can therefore silently change untouched roles. Reproduction command: bun -e 'const s = await Bun.file("ui/components/RetryModels.tsx").text(); const e = s.match(/const groups = (.*);/)[1]; console.log(new Function("r", "role", "complexity", "return " + e)({effective:{triage:{small:{groups:["small/model"]},large:{groups:["large/model"]}}}}, "triage", "large"));' Output: [ "large/model" ]. The pipeline would select small/model.
findings.failure_scenario: A large run has no saved model overrides and routing has different triage.small and triage.large chains. Retrying after editing only implement submits triage.large as an override, replacing the triage.small chain that the pipeline actually uses.

findings.title: Clearing default effort does not clear the persisted value
findings.detail: An empty effort field omits effort from PATCH. RuntimeCatalog.patch merges the patch over the existing model, so the old effort survives despite a successful save. It also prevents removing that effort from supportedEfforts, because validation still sees the old default. Reproduction command: bun -e 'const s = await Bun.file("ui/components/CatalogForm.tsx").text(); const e = s.match(/\.\.\.\(f\.effort[^\n]+/)[0].slice(3).replace(/,$/, ""); const patch = new Function("f", "return " + e)({effort:""}); console.log({...{effort:"high"}, ...patch});' Output: { effort: "high" }.
findings.failure_scenario: Edit a runtime model with default effort high, erase Default effort and save. Reopening the editor shows high again, and routing continues to use it.

findings.title: Catalog history disappears when Setup is closed
findings.detail: Catalog history is populated only by local mutation callbacks into a component signal. Navigating away or reloading erases it, and catalog changes received through SSE never enter it. This does not provide the requested recent catalog changes alongside routing history.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or delete a runtime model, navigate to Models, then return to Setup. Catalog history is empty. Changes made by another operator are also absent despite the catalog updating over SSE.

findings.detail: For runs without overrides, opening this picker converts every effective policy chain into an explicit run override. Submitting after changing only the implementer therefore also pins review, holdout, and verification. Explicit chains bypass independence ranking and verification checkpoint exclusions. A direct check produced {"normalReview":"codex/sol","retryPrefilledReview":"claude/opus"}. findings.failure_scenario: Retry a large run with models={}, change only the implementer to claude/opus, and submit. The untouched review role is also pinned and can select claude/opus instead of the independent Codex reviewer.

findings.title: Clearing a runtime model's default effort does not persist
findings.detail: When the effort field is cleared, the PATCH payload omits effort. RuntimeCatalog.patch merges that payload over the existing model, so the old effort survives. The UI reports success while retaining the value the operator removed. Removing that effort from supportedEfforts at the same time instead causes validation to reject the edit.
findings.failure_scenario: Edit a runtime model with effort="high", clear Default effort, and save. Reopening the editor still shows "high".

findings.title: Catalog history disappears on navigation and misses external changes
findings.detail: The requested recent catalog history is implemented only as component-local session state, populated by this page's mutation callbacks. Navigating away or reloading erases it. Catalog changes received over SSE refresh the catalog but never enter history, so changes from another browser or API client are absent.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or delete a runtime model, navigate away from Setup, and return. Catalog history is empty even though the catalog change remains. An external catalog edit is never recorded here.

gold.summary: Digest actions are derived from stale records instead of current unanswered and review state.
A historical failed review hides a later approval in MCP status.

findings.title: Answered questions remain in the needs-you digest
findings.detail: Answering a question emits no clearing feed event, so replaying run.question keeps an answered question actionable until the run finishes. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-354.ts"` against an in-memory Store printed `answered question: expected Needs you: 0; actual Needs you: 1; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0`, despite zero open questions and a running run.
findings.failure_scenario: A question is answered through the UI or another consumer, the run resumes, and the digest consumer has not acknowledged the original question.

findings.title: Active fix rounds still appear as awaiting review
findings.detail: The digest ignores review.round_started, leaving the original PR-opened item in the review queue while changes are being implemented. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-354.ts"` with a real Store-created review round printed `active review round: expected PRs awaiting review: 0; actual Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0`.
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer submits changes, creating a queued or running fix round, then starts another session before that round delivers.

findings.title: Merged PRs remain listed as blocked lands
findings.detail: Blocked lands are cleared only by another queue attempt or land.landed. External merges produce run.merged/pr.merged instead, leaving a completed PR actionable indefinitely. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-354.ts"` after Store.resolveMergedRun printed `externally merged blocked land: expected Blocked lands: 0; actual Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 1`.
findings.failure_scenario: Landing blocks on CI, a human fixes and merges the PR outside the queue, and the next digest includes both the blocked event and confirmed merge event.

findings.title: Status discards the persisted merged flag
findings.detail: The status schema strips run.merged, and the landed check never examines it. Store.resolveMergedRun deliberately preserves succeeded status while setting merged=true, so a confirmed merge without a saved PR snapshot or landed entry is reported as unknown. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-354.ts"` printed `persisted merge: expected Landed; actual PR state unknown`.
findings.failure_scenario: Merge reconciliation confirms an externally merged succeeded run using the fallback PR client, while no saved PR snapshot or land entry exists.

findings.title: Historical round failures override a newer valid approval
findings.detail: A failed or cancelled last round returns before the current approval is considered. The existing review API permits approving the current head after such a round, but status continues directing the agent to inspect the failed round instead of landing. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-354.ts"` printed `approved after failed round: expected Approved; landing not queued; actual Review changes failed`.
findings.failure_scenario: A fix round fails, a human fixes the PR manually and approves its current SHA through limitless_review, then calls limitless_status.

gold.summary: Digest actions are derived from stale records instead of current unanswered and review state.
A historical failed review hides a later approval in MCP status.

findings.title: Stale approvals permanently hide PRs that need another review
findings.detail: review.approved removes the PR from the digest, but a subsequent head change invalidates the approval without generating another run.pr_opened or review.round_delivered event. The digest consequently reports no review needed even though the recorded approval is stale. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {Store} from "./src/db/store.ts"; import {digestCommand} from "./src/cli/digest.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); const repo=s.upsertRepo({slug:"o/r",kind:"github",url:null,localPath:null,defaultBranch:"main",mergePolicy:"pr"}); const r=s.createRun(repo,{repo:"o/r",prompt:"work"}); const url="https://github.com/o/r/pull/1"; s.updateRun(r.id,{status:"succeeded",prUrl:url}); s.observePrHead(
findings.failure_scenario: A PR is approved, then someone pushes another commit outside a factory review round. A new session sees zero PRs awaiting review.

findings.title: Answered questions remain listed as needing user attention
findings.detail: Answering a question and returning to running emits none of the listed clearing events. The digest therefore continues presenting the answered question until the run finishes. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {Store} from "./src/db/store.ts"; import {digestCommand} from "./src/cli/digest.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); const repo=s.upsertRepo({slug:"o/r",kind:"github",url:null,localPath:null,defaultBranch:"main",mergePolicy:"pr"}); const r=s.createRun(repo,{repo:"o/r",prompt:"work"}); const q=s.askQuestion(r.id,"Which option?"); s.answerQuestion(q.id,"A","human"); s.updateRun(r.id,{status:"running"}); await digestCommand([],{}, {api:async()=>s.readFeed({limit:1000}),print:console.log
findings.failure_scenario: A human answers an outstanding question without acknowledging that consumer's feed cursor; the run resumes and a later session digest asks for attention on the already answered question.

findings.title: Preserve exclusion reasons when remaining verifiers cannot verify
findings.detail: Exclusion reasons are reported only when filtering empties the roster. Exclusions can therefore remove the only usable verifier without the required origin-excluded reason appearing in the failure or run log.

gold.summary: A pinned candidate slot deadline exits without recording the chain-exhaustion question.

findings.title: Preserve exclusions for previously attempted verifiers
findings.detail: Pinned verify routing unconditionally clears excludeModels. The environment-blocked retry passes the first verifier through this constraint specifically to obtain another verifier (engine.ts:1553). Clearing it selects the first chain entry again, consuming the only retry without trying an available second model. This exclusion concerns a previous verification attempt, not the soft preference against the implementer's checkpoint.
findings.failure_scenario: A run pins verify to [A, B]. A returns an environment-blocked result, while B would pass. The retry discards the exclusion of A, invokes A again, and moves the run to needs_human without invoking B.

findings.title: Include pinned-chain diagnostics when routing times out
findings.detail: Only the empty-candidate branch creates the required operator question. Deadline expiration here or after admission throws a generic NoCapacityError without recording the chain or candidate skip reasons. Pinned local production reviewers now propagate these errors instead of being skipped, so they can leave a run in needs_human without the requested recovery question.
findings.failure_scenario: A pinned production panel reviewer waits for a busy provider until its local finder deadline expires. The run enters needs_human with a busy/deadline error but no question identifying its pinned chain and candidate reasons.

findings.title: Preserve the failed verifier exclusion when using a pinned chain
findings.detail: Pinned verify calls unconditionally clear excludeModels. The environment-blocked retry passes the first verifier through this constraint specifically to obtain another checkpoint, so clearing it selects the same model again even when another chain candidate is available. An isolated fake-harness check, `bun "$TMPDIR/review-pinned-retry.ts"`, produced: {"excludedAfterEnvironmentBlock":"a","expectedRetryModel":"b","actualRetryModel":"a"}.
findings.failure_scenario: A run pins verify to ["a", "b"]. Model a reports only environment-blocked criteria. The retry excludes a, but invoke removes that exclusion and calls a again. If a remains blocked while b could verify successfully, the run unnecessarily enters needs_human.

findings.title: Reconcile reruns whose POST response was lost
findings.detail: Reconciliation only considers rerunning rows. If GitHub accepts the POST but its response is lost, or the daemon stops before finishCiFailure, the persisted row remains rerun_requested. A subsequent successful attempt is ignored, and SUCCESS clears pending inspection without recording flake evidence. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: Expected: "failed_then_passed"; Received: "rerun_requested". The confirmed-rerun control passed.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts the rerun, the connection resets before its 201 response arrives, and attempt 2 succeeds at the original SHA.

findings.title: Resume suppressed PR inspection when main recovers
findings.detail: Main-red suppression completes inspection and clears ciPending. Subsequent unchanged PR snapshots never inspect main again, so recovery of the default branch cannot resume the suppressed reaction. Even another PR updating the repository's main-red state does not schedule this PR. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-poller-review.test.ts". The recovery probe output was: Expected length: 1; Received length: 0.
findings.failure_scenario: A timed-out PR check is suppressed because main fails the same check. Main subsequently becomes green while the PR's failed snapshot remains unchanged; its eligible rerun never happens.

findings.title: Isolate CI inspection errors to the affected PR
findings.detail: An exception from classifyCi propagates out of record and aborts the repository's entire observation loop. Because tracked PRs have stable ordering and failed inspections remain pending, a persistent detail failure on the first PR repeatedly prevents later PRs from being observed, including merge and closure changes. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-poller-review.test.ts". Output: "GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI log" twice; the assertion that PR 2 had saved observation data failed with Received: null.
findings.failure_scenario: The first tracked PR repeatedly receives unavailable or malformed CI logs. A second tracked PR in the same repository never has its GraphQL snapshot recorded.

findings.title: Reconcile rerun requests whose POST response was lost
findings.detail: Only rows marked rerunning are reconciled. If GitHub accepts the POST but its response is lost, the persisted row remains rerun_requested. A subsequent passing rerun is ignored, permanently losing the required flake evidence. Running `bun run "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` produced: `lost POST response then passing rerun: expected failed_then_passed; actual rerun_requested`.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a job rerun, the connection drops before its 201 response reaches the poller, and the rerun passes at the same SHA.

findings.title: Find the rerun job across workflow attempts
findings.detail: Reconciliation searches only the workflow's latest attempt. Attempt-specific job lists can omit jobs rerun in an earlier attempt. If another job is subsequently rerun, the original job has zero matches and classification throws indefinitely, leaving its ledger outcome unresolved. Running `bun run "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` produced: `origin rerun completed in attempt 2; unrelated job rerun created attempt 3: actual Error: Ambiguous CI rerun job ledger rerunning`.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory reruns job A in attempt 2. Before the next poll, another job in the workflow is rerun in attempt 3. Attempt 3's job list excludes A.

findings.title: Deduplicate main-red notifications at repository scope
findings.detail: The notification key includes the check name, so simultaneous failures of different checks create separate ci.main_red items for the same repository. findings.title: Reconcile reruns whose POST response was lost
findings.detail: The reconciliation loop only handles outcome rerunning. A crash or lost response after GitHub accepts the POST leaves rerun_requested, which is never inspected for later-attempt evidence. A subsequent successful rollup completes inspection without recording the flake; a failed observation instead marks it failed_again without establishing the rerun result. findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a rerun, but its response is lost or the daemon exits before finishCiFailure sets rerunning. After restart, attempt 2 passes at the same SHA. The ledger remains rerun_requested permanently instead of recording failed_then_passed.

findings.title: Resume suppressed PR failures when main recovers
findings.detail: Main-red suppression completes the inspection and clears ciPending. Subsequent polls skip classification while the PR's GraphQL state remains unchanged, so recovery of main never resumes the PR reaction. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` reproduced: `main recovered, unchanged PR: {"reruns":0,"needsFix":0,"mainReads":1,"ciPending":false}`.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR job times out while the same check fails on main. Main subsequently becomes green, but the PR remains red at the same SHA. The PR receives neither its transient rerun nor ci.needs_fix, indefinitely.

findings.title: Reconcile rerun requests with ambiguous responses
findings.detail: Reconciliation excludes rerun_requested rows. If GitHub accepts the POST but its response is lost, the persisted claim remains rerun_requested. A subsequent success clears inspection without recording the flake; a still-red observation can instead label it failed_again without inspecting the rerun. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` reproduced: `accepted rerun whose response was lost, then same-SHA pass: {"outcome":"rerun_requested","runLookups":0,"ciPending":false}`.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a job rerun, the connection resets before the 201 response arrives, and that rerun passes at the original SHA. The ledger never records failed_then_passed, including after restart.

gold.summary: A definitively refused CI rerun remains pending indefinitely.
Passing security-test output incorrectly prevents a transient CI rerun.

findings.title: Resolve rerun claims when GitHub definitively rejects the request
findings.detail: The rerun claim is persisted before the POST, but a rejected POST only throws. Subsequent inspections wait for run_attempt to advance and suppress needs-fix because the claim remains pending. A rejected request never creates that later attempt, so classification stays pending indefinitely. Reproduction command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-o0sYkW/claude-501/ci-review.ts`. Output: `first inspection: Error: CI job rerun was not confirmed`, followed by three `later inspection complete: false` lines and `{"posts":1,"outcome":"rerun_requested","needsFix":0}`.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub returns HTTP 422 to the rerun POST. The originating workflow remains on attempt 1 forever, and every later inspection leaves the ledger in rerun_requested without emitting ci.needs_fix.

findings.title: Isolate CI inspection failures to the affected PR
findings.detail: Classifier exceptions escape record() and abort the repository's entire observation loop. Later PRs are skipped even though their GraphQL snapshots were fetched successfully. The same ordering repeats on subsequent polls, so a persistent CI-detail error can indefinitely suppress merge, close, review, and CI observations for other PRs. Reproduction command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-o0sYkW/claude-501/ci-review-poller.ts`. Output: `{"firstPrSaves":2,"secondPrSaves":0,"logs":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: commits/main (500)","GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: commits/main (500)"]}`.
findings.failure_scenario: Two PRs are tracked in one repository. The first has failed CI and its CI REST inspection returns HTTP 500; the second has a valid passing or merged snapshot. Every poll aborts on the first PR before saving the second.

findings.title: Definitively rejected reruns remain pending forever
findings.detail: The rerun is claimed before POST, but every non-201 response leaves it in rerun_requested. If GitHub rejects the request, no later attempt exists to resolve that claim. Subsequent inspections suppress ci.needs_fix and keep polling indefinitely. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` with a fake 422 response produced `reject Error: CI job rerun was not confirmed`, followed by `reject {"outcomes":["rerun_requested"],"feed":[],"reruns":1,"mainStatusesRequested":false}` after three inspections.
findings.failure_scenario: A transient job qualifies for rerun, but GitHub returns 422 without starting another attempt. All later observations retain the original run_attempt, leaving the failure permanently pending without actionable classification.

findings.title: Inspect main's commit statuses independently of the PR's context types
findings.detail: The shared checks helper fetches legacy commit statuses only when the PR snapshot contains status contexts or is truncated. Main can publish a failing legacy status with the same name as the PR's Actions check, so this condition hides main's failure and incorrectly permits a rerun. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` against that fixture produced `main-status {"outcomes":["rerunning"],"feed":[],"reruns":1,"mainStatusesRequested":false}`.
findings.failure_scenario: Main has a failing legacy commit status named test, while the factory PR has a timed-out Actions check named test and no legacy status contexts. The classifier reruns the PR job and emits no ci.main_red item.

gold.summary: A definitively refused CI rerun remains pending indefinitely.
Passing security-test output incorrectly prevents a transient CI rerun.

findings.title: Rejected rerun requests remain pending forever
findings.detail: The rerun is claimed before the POST, but a definitive rejection leaves its outcome as rerun_requested. Subsequent inspections wait for a newer run_attempt that will never exist, suppressing ci.needs_fix indefinitely. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-pKEV2z/claude-501/review-ci.ts`. Output: `first rejected request: Error: CI job rerun was not confirmed`; three subsequent inspections returned false; final result was `{"posts":1,"outcome":"rerun_requested","needsFix":0}`.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub returns HTTP 422 to the job rerun POST and the workflow remains at its original attempt.

findings.title: One CI inspection error starves other PRs in the repository
findings.detail: Classifier exceptions escape record() and abort the repository's entire observation loop. The failing PR retains ciPending and is retried first every cycle, preventing later PRs from recording CI, reviews, or merge state. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-pKEV2z/claude-501/review-poller.ts`. After three cycles, output was `"savedPrs": [1,1,1], "secondPrObserved": false`, with `Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)` logged each cycle.
findings.failure_scenario: The first tracked PR has deleted or unavailable job logs returning 404; a second PR in the same repository has a valid observation.

findings.title: Job reruns can also rerun downstream security tests
findings.detail: GitHub's job rerun endpoint reruns the selected job and its dependent jobs. The security checks inspect only the selected job; the sibling lookup also filters immediately to that job's name. Consequently, a permitted transient rerun can automatically rerun a downstream security job, violating the security-test exclusion.
findings.failure_scenario: A timed-out unit-test job has a dependent security-test job using `needs` and `if: always()`. Rerunning the unit-test job also reruns the security job.

findings.title: Recognize test timeout diagnostics beyond Bun and Playwright
findings.detail: The anchored timeout expression excludes legitimate test-owned timeout messages such as Node's `test timed out after 100ms`. These failures are classified as needing a fix instead of receiving the requested transient retry. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-pKEV2z/claude-501/review-ci.ts`. Output: `Node test timeout result: {"posts":0,"outcome":"failed","needsFix":1}`.
findings.failure_scenario: An Actions job concludes failure and its log contains the Node test-runner diagnostic `test timed out after 100ms`.

findings.title: Resolve definitively rejected reruns instead of waiting forever
findings.detail: The rerun is claimed before the POST, but every non-201 response throws without resolving that claim. If GitHub explicitly rejects the request, subsequent inspections see run_attempt unchanged and retain rerun_requested indefinitely, emitting no ci.needs_fix. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: after explicit HTTP 403: {"outcomes":["rerun_requested"],"feed":[]}; assertion Expected: true, Received: false.
findings.failure_scenario: A timed-out job is eligible for retry, but the token lacks Actions write permission and the rerun POST returns HTTP 403. GitHub never starts another attempt, leaving classification pending permanently.

findings.title: Record main-red failures before suppressing PR reactions
findings.detail: The main-red branch continues before fetching the job evidence or recording the failure. Consequently, these failures never enter the ledger, despite the requirement to record each failure signature, SHA, runner image, and outcome. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: main-red inspection: {"ledgerRows":0,...}; assertion Expected: 1, Received: 0.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory PR has a failed test check and main has the same failing check. Classification emits ci.main_red but creates no ci_failures row for the PR SHA.

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: Unaccepted rerun requests remain pending forever
findings.detail: A 429, network failure before submission, or crash between claiming and posting leaves outcome rerun_requested. When GitHub never creates another attempt, reconciliation always continues here, and the pending prior record suppresses ci.needs_fix indefinitely. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: after 100 reconciliation polls {"complete":false,"posts":1,"outcome":"rerun_requested","needsFix":0}; Expected: true, Received: false.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub rejects the rerun with HTTP 429 and run_attempt remains 1, or the daemon crashes after claiming but before sending the POST.

findings.title: Lagging check data reports a confirmed passing rerun as needing a fix
findings.detail: Successful reconciliation adds only the new job ID to resolved. If the check-runs endpoint still returns the original failed job, that ID is not skipped. The prior failed_then_passed record prevents another rerun but falls through to needsFix, producing contradictory ledger and feed results. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: successful rerun with lagging checks {"outcome":"failed_then_passed","feed":["ci.needs_fix"]}; Expected: false, Received: true.
findings.failure_scenario: A pending inspection observes attempt 2 succeeding through the workflow jobs API while GraphQL and the commit check-runs endpoint still expose attempt 1's failure.

findings.title: Main-red suppression bypasses the failure ledger
findings.detail: The main-red branch continues before fetching job evidence, constructing the signature, or recording the failure. Consequently, these failures have no ledger record despite the requirement to record each failure signature, SHA, and outcome. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: main-red result {"ledgerRows":0,...}; Expected: 1, Received: 0.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory PR's non-security test job fails while the default branch is red on the same check; ci.main_red is emitted, but ci_failures remains empty.

findings.title: Rate-limited rerun requests remain pending forever
findings.detail: A rejected 429 response leaves the durable claim as rerun_requested. Subsequent inspections wait for run_attempt to increase, but GitHub never accepted the rerun, so neither a retry nor ci.needs_fix occurs. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` produced `{"name":"rate-limit-rejection","posts":1,"outcomes":["rerun_requested"],"needsFix":0,"error":"Error: CI job rerun was not confirmed"}` after four inspections.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub rejects the rerun POST with HTTP 429; the workflow remains at its original attempt across subsequent polls and restarts.

findings.title: One CI inspection failure starves later PR observations
findings.detail: Classifier exceptions escape record and terminate the repository's observation loop. Because ciPending remains persisted, the same PR repeats the failure every poll and prevents later PRs from recording CI, review, closure, or merge observations. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-poller-review.ts"` across three polls saved only `https://github.com/o/r/pull/1`; each poll logged `Incomplete CI inspection: commits/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa/check-runs?filter=latest&per_page=100&page=1 (404)`.
findings.failure_scenario: The first tracked PR repeatedly returns unavailable or malformed CI details while a later PR has valid GraphQL observations.

findings.title: Case-sensitive API URL validation rejects valid repositories
findings.detail: Repository registration preserves the user's slug casing, while GitHub returns canonical casing in check_run_url. This strict comparison rejects a legitimate job even though the preceding details_url comparison accepts case differences. The rerun reconciliation prefix check has the same problem. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` with stored `o/r` and returned `O/R` produced `{"name":"canonical-repo-case","posts":0,"outcomes":[],"needsFix":0,"error":"Error: Incomplete failing job"}`.
findings.failure_scenario: A repository is registered using lowercase owner/name, but GitHub's canonical owner or repository name contains uppercase characters.

findings.title: Test timeout classification excludes the requested diagnostic
findings.detail: Only three hardcoded diagnostic formats qualify. An actual failure line such as `error: smoke timed out after 30000ms` is classified as needs-fix despite matching the requested test timeout case. The added tests explicitly expect this exclusion. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` produced `{"name":"test-own-timeout","posts":0,"outcomes":["failed"],"needsFix":4,"error":""}`.
findings.failure_scenario: A test runner reports its own timeout as `error: smoke timed out after 30000ms` and the Actions job concludes failure.

findings.title: Main-branch status lookup depends on the PR's context types
findings.detail: The shared checks function fetches legacy commit statuses only when the PR snapshot contains StatusContext entries or is truncated. Consequently, a failing main status is invisible when the PR exposes the same check through CheckRun. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` with a failing main status named test produced `{"name":"main-red-legacy-status","posts":1,"mainStatusReads":0,"outcomes":["rerunning"],"needsFix":0,"error":""}`.
findings.failure_scenario: Main reports a failing legacy commit status named test, while the factory PR reports test through the Checks API.

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: ANSI colors bypass security-failure and timeout detection
findings.detail: Log normalization removes timestamps but preserves ANSI escapes. The anchored security and timeout patterns consequently miss colored diagnostics. A generic timed-out job containing a colored '(fail) security tests' line is rerun and recorded in the ledger, violating the security-test exclusion. Colored timeout diagnostics also fail transient classification. Running `bun /private/tmp/lr-MP54Mh/claude-501/ci-review.ts` produced `FAIL a colored security failure is excluded from reruns and ledger` with `1 !== 0`, and the colored-timeout assertion produced `0 !== 1`.
findings.failure_scenario: An Actions job named 'test' times out and its logs contain '\u001b[31m(fail)\u001b[0m security tests'; its steps and annotations provide no other security-specific evidence.

findings.title: Later partial attempts strand tracked rerun results
findings.detail: Reconciliation searches only the latest workflow attempt. GitHub partial reruns can omit jobs completed in earlier attempts, so a later rerun of another job makes the tracked job disappear from this query permanently. Every subsequent inspection throws instead of recording its result. Running `bun /private/tmp/lr-MP54Mh/claude-501/ci-review.ts` produced `FAIL a tracked rerun is reconciled after a later partial attempt: Error: Ambiguous CI rerun job`.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory reruns job A from attempt 1; A passes in attempt 2. Before polling, another failed job B is rerun in attempt 3, whose jobs response contains only B.

findings.title: Rate-limited rerun requests remain claimed forever
findings.detail: A rate-limit refusal leaves the row as 'rerun_requested'. After cooldown, reconciliation sees no newer workflow attempt, and the pending-prior branch prevents both another POST and ci.needs_fix. This permanently stalls classification even though GitHub never started a rerun. Running `bun /private/tmp/lr-MP54Mh/claude-501/ci-review.ts` produced `FAIL a rate-limited POST must eventually rerun or report needs-fix: AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: posts=1, outcome=rerun_requested, needs_fix=0` after three further inspections.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub returns HTTP 429 for the rerun POST, then recovers. The original failed workflow remains at attempt 1.

findings.title: Main-red failures bypass the failure ledger
findings.detail: The main-red branch continues before job inspection and recordCiFailure, so these PR failures never receive the required signature, runner image, SHA, and outcome record. Pausing reactions should not discard failure evidence. Running `bun /private/tmp/lr-MP54Mh/claude-501/ci-review.ts` produced `FAIL a main-red failure is still recorded in the failure ledger` with `0 !== 1`.
findings.failure_scenario: Both the default branch and a factory PR fail the non-security check 'test'; the classifier emits ci.main_red but creates no ledger row for the PR failure.

findings.title: Isolate CI inspection failures to the affected PR
findings.detail: A classifier exception escapes record(), aborting observation of every later PR in the repository. A persistent missing log therefore starves unrelated PRs indefinitely. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: starvation {"secondSnapshot":null,"logs":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)","GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)"]}; assertion expected secondSnapshot not to be null.
findings.failure_scenario: Two tracked PRs share a repository. The first has a failed job whose logs return 404. The second never receives a saved observation, including subsequent merge, close, review, or CI changes.

findings.title: Resolve claims when rate limiting rejects the rerun
findings.detail: A rejected HTTP 429 leaves rerun_requested permanently claimed. Because no rerun actually started, run_attempt never advances; reconciliation neither retries nor emits ci.needs_fix. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output after cooldown and eight further polls: rate-limited claim {"outcome":"rerun_requested","reruns":1,"needsFix":0}; assertion expected outcome not to remain rerun_requested.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub returns 429 to the rerun POST, then becomes available again. The workflow remains on its original failed attempt forever, with no rerun or needs-fix result.

findings.title: Search intervening attempts when reconciling a rerun
findings.detail: Reconciliation examines only the latest workflow attempt. Attempt-specific job listings omit jobs that were not rerun in that attempt, so a subsequent partial rerun can permanently hide the factory's completed attempt. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: partial-rerun {"outcome":"rerunning","logs":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Ambiguous CI rerun job","GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Ambiguous CI rerun job"]}; expected failed_then_passed.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory reruns job A in attempt 2 and it passes. Before the next poll, someone reruns unrelated job B in attempt 3. The classifier never reads A's passing attempt and keeps its ledger row pending.

findings.title: Observe rerun completion beyond the first 100 contexts
findings.detail: An outstanding rerun triggers inspection only when ciChanged is true. The query observes just the first 100 contexts, while REST can discover and rerun checks outside that page. Completion of such a check can leave ciKey unchanged indefinitely. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: hidden rerun {"outcome":"rerunning","additionalRestCalls":0}; expected failed_then_passed.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR has 101 checks. A visible check keeps the rollup red, and the hidden check is rerun successfully. Neither the first 100 contexts nor the rollup changes, so the passing rerun is never recorded.

findings.title: Recognize standard security-test failure diagnostics
findings.detail: The security exclusion misses standard Go failure lines such as '--- FAIL: TestSecurity (0.00s)'. A generic timed-out job containing that failure is rerun and entered in the ledger, violating the security-test exclusion. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: security reruns {"reruns":1,"ledger":[..."outcome":"rerunning"...]}; assertion expected zero reruns.
findings.failure_scenario: A job named test times out after reporting a failed TestSecurity test. Its steps have generic names and there are no annotations. The classifier automatically reruns the security failure.

findings.title: Record failures suppressed by red main in the ledger
findings.detail: The main-red branch continues before fetching job evidence or recording the failure. These failures never receive the requested signature, runner image, SHA, or outcome in the ledger. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: main-red ledger []; assertion expected length 1, received length 0.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory PR fails the same check as main. The repository notification is emitted, but its failure is absent from the ledger; pushing a new SHA before main recovers loses the observation permanently.

gold.summary: Catalog mutation can invalidate a shadowed retained policy and prevent the daemon from restarting.

findings.title: Allow PATCH to clear an optional default effort
findings.detail: Omitting effort preserves the old value, while sending null fails validation. Consequently, an existing runtime model cannot be updated to use backend-default effort, which is needed for Claude-backed agent roles. Direct reproduction command: bun -e 'import {RuntimeCatalog} from "./src/router/runtime-catalog.ts"; import {MODELS,PROVIDERS} from "./src/router/catalog.ts"; const m={...MODELS[0],id:"claude/exp",source:"runtime",effort:"high",supportedEfforts:["high"]}; const c=new RuntimeCatalog({},[m],PROVIDERS,{getPolicy:()=>({})},{}); try {c.patch(m.id,{effort:null});} catch(e) {console.log(String(e));}' Output: Error: model.effort: invalid or missing field
findings.failure_scenario: Add an omlx runtime model with default effort none, then attempt to update it for implement routing without a default effort. PATCH cannot express that valid model definition; deletion and recreation are required.

findings.title: Clear stale model rejection blocks when replacing a backend
findings.detail: Catalog mutations update model definitions but leave ProviderTracker.modelBlocks keyed by the unchanged catalog ID. After a backend rejection, correcting its backend through PATCH still leaves the corrected model unroutable for up to 24 hours. Deleting and re-adding that ID also retains the block. An in-memory add → blockModel → patch → route check printed `resolved backend: good-build` followed by `{"candidates":[],"skipped":[{"modelId":"codex/experiment","reason":"codex: model rejected: unknown model bad-build"}]}`.
findings.failure_scenario: Add codex/experiment with backend bad-build, invoke it and receive an unknown-model rejection, then PATCH its model field to good-build. Explicit run chains and policy cells still skip the corrected model because the old rejection block survives.

gold.summary: Catalog mutation can invalidate a shadowed retained policy and prevent the daemon from restarting.

findings.title: Clear stale backend rejection when replacing a runtime model
findings.detail: Catalog updates replace the router definition but retain ProviderTracker.modelBlocks, which are keyed only by catalog ID. A rejection of the old backend therefore blocks the replacement backend for up to 24 hours. Deleting and re-adding the ID also retains the block. Check: `bun "$TMPDIR/catalog-review.ts" block` printed `{"candidates":[],"skipped":[{"modelId":"codex/experiment","reason":"codex: model rejected: old-build is not available"}]}` and failed with `AssertionError: patched new backend must not inherit old backend rejection` (`0 !== 1`).
findings.failure_scenario: A runtime model targeting old-build receives a model rejection. The operator patches its backend to an available new-build and explicitly routes to it. Routing still skips it because of old-build's rejection.

findings.title: Prevent older probes from overwriting newer discovery results
findings.detail: Each probe unconditionally records its response without request ordering or a generation check. Concurrent probes can finish out of order, persisting an obsolete served set and making the router reject a currently served model. Provider enable operations can start probes alongside scheduled probes. Check: `bun "$TMPDIR/catalog-review.ts" ordering` printed `{"served":["retired-build"],"candidates":[],"skipped":[{"modelId":"omlx/qwen-flash","reason":"not served by omlx"}]}` and failed with `AssertionError: late older probe must not overwrite newer served list` (`0 !== 1`).
findings.failure_scenario: An older probe captures the previous backend list. A second probe observes the replacement model and completes first. The older response then arrives and replaces the current discovery result, so routing skips the replacement until another successful probe.

gold.summary: Effort removal is persisted without checking policy cells hidden by operator overrides.

findings.title: Validate runtime mutations against the underlying eval policy
findings.detail: PATCH validates only the effective policy, so an operator override can hide an eval-policy reference that the patch invalidates. Resetting that override then produces no eligible candidate. On restart, Factory reads and validates the eval policy before applying operator overrides, so startup fails. DELETE similarly checks only operator cells and accepts deletion of an eval-policy model. Reproduction command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-pqEs0s/claude-501/catalog-review.XXXXXX.ts`. Output: `PATCH accepted\nrestart policy INVALID: Unsupported effort high\n{"candidates":[],"skipped":[{"modelId":"codex/experiment@high","reason":"Error: Unsupported effort \"high\" for codex/experiment; supported: none"}]
findings.failure_scenario: Add codex/experiment supporting high and none; load an eval policy naming codex/experiment@high; override that cell with codex/sol; PATCH the experiment to support only none. The patch succeeds, resetting the override breaks routing, and restarting rejects the eval policy. Deleting the experiment al

findings.title: Deleting a file-policy model prevents daemon restart
findings.detail: Deletion checks only persisted operator cells. A runtime model referenced by routing/policy.json can therefore be deleted successfully, but Factory subsequently calls readPolicy against the reduced catalog and throws during startup. Direct reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-catalog.ts". Output: "DELETE succeeded\nrestart failed: routing/policy.json references deleted codex/experiment". The fixture installs a valid file-backed policy, deletes its runtime model, then repeats startup policy validation.
findings.failure_scenario: Add codex/experiment, reference it in routing/policy.json, load that policy, delete the model without any operator cell referencing it, then restart the daemon.

findings.title: Older probes can overwrite newer discovery results
findings.detail: Probe results are committed without a per-provider generation check or serialization. Probes can overlap because setEnabled starts a probe even when another is pending. An older response arriving last replaces the newer served set and persists it with a fresh observation timestamp. Direct reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-discovery.ts". Output: "served: [\"old-build\"]\nnew-build rejected: true". The fixture resolves the second fake probe with new-build before resolving the first with old-build.
findings.failure_scenario: A scheduled probe observes old-build but responds slowly. An enable request starts another probe after the backend changes; it returns new-build first. The older response then overwrites discovery, causing current models to be skipped until another successful probe.
