findings.title: Backend edits retain the previous model's rejection block
findings.failure_scenario: An invocation rejects old-build as unavailable. The operator PATCHes the same runtime catalog ID to a working new-build, or deletes and re-adds that ID. Explicit policy cells and run chains still skip it because of the old rejection.

findings.title: An older probe can overwrite newer discovery results
findings.failure_scenario: A scheduled probe captures old-build. After the server switches builds, enabling the provider triggers another probe that reports new-build first. The delayed older response then restores old-build, causing the router to skip the working new-build and admit the removed backend until another successf

findings.title: Validate catalog patches against shadowed policy layers
findings.detail: PATCH validates only the effective policy, so an operator override can hide an evals policy reference that the patch invalidates. Resetting the override then restores an invalid policy; restarting also fails when Factory reads and validates the evals policy against the persisted model. Reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/catalog-hidden-policy.ts". Output: "PATCH accepted efforts=[none] while evals references @high", followed by "AssertionError: Got unwanted exception: Reset must restore a valid policy" and "Unsupported effort \"high\" for codex/experiment; supported: none".
findings.failure_scenario: An evals policy names codex/experiment@high. An operator overrides that cell with codex/sol. PATCH removes high from the runtime model's supported efforts and succeeds. Clearing the operator override restores the unsupported target, and the persisted change prevents subsequent startup.

gold.summary: Retrying an unchanged run converts inherited model chains into explicit overrides.
Routing previews remain stale after quota or cooldown expiry without an event.
Clearing a default effort omits the field from PATCH and leaves the old value stored.
Catalog history disappears on reload and does not include changes made by another client.

findings.title: Clearing default effort silently preserves the saved value
findings.detail: An empty Default effort field omits effort from the PATCH. RuntimeCatalog.patch merges the patch over the existing model, so the old effort survives despite a successful save. A direct Bun execution of the extracted submit handler produced a patch without effort and effortAfterBackendMerge:"high". Removing high from supported efforts at the same time instead makes the edit fail validation.
findings.failure_scenario: Edit a runtime model with effort high, clear Default effort, and save. Reopening the editor still shows high.

findings.title: Catalog history disappears when Setup is reopened
findings.detail: Catalog history renders only the component-local session signal, populated by this component's mutation callbacks. Navigating away or refreshing erases all entries. Changes from another browser or API client never appear, even after catalog SSE refreshes. This does not provide the requested recent catalog-change history.
findings.failure_scenario: Add, edit, or delete a runtime model, navigate to Models, and return to Setup. The catalog history is empty despite the saved change.

findings.title: Failed routing load leaves the retry picker permanently loading
findings.detail: The rejection handler sets an error but never clears loading or offers a reload action. The picker remains hidden and submission remains disabled after the request has finished. Recovery requires cancelling and reopening the panel.
findings.failure_scenario: Open Retry with different models for a run without explicit chains while GET /api/routing fails once. Even after connectivity recovers, the open panel remains stuck on Loading current routing.

findings.title: Catalog history only records changes made during the current mount
findings.detail: The requested recent catalog history is replaced with a local session signal. It is populated only by this page's mutation callbacks, is erased on navigation or reload, and never records changes received over SSE. Consequently operators cannot inspect recent catalog changes made elsewhere or before opening Setup.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or delete a runtime model, navigate away from Setup, and return. The catalog change history is empty. Changes made by another client likewise never appear.

gold.summary: Retrying an unchanged run converts inherited model chains into explicit overrides.
Routing previews remain stale after quota or cooldown expiry without an event.
Clearing a default effort omits the field from PATCH and leaves the old value stored.
Catalog history disappears on reload and does not include changes made by another client.

findings.title: Clearing the default effort silently preserves its previous value
findings.detail: An empty effort input omits effort from the PATCH payload. RuntimeCatalog.patch merges that payload over the existing model, retaining its previous effort. Saving therefore reports success without applying the edit. A diagnostic executing the extracted payload expression and backend merge returned {"payloadHasEffort":false,"resultingEffortAfterPatchMerge":"high"}.
findings.failure_scenario: Edit a runtime model whose default effort is high, clear Default effort, and save. The model still defaults to high. Removing high from supported efforts at the same time instead causes validation to reject the update.

findings.title: Catalog history disappears when Setup is reopened
findings.detail: The requested recent catalog history is replaced with a page-local session signal. Only mutations made through this mounted page call record(); catalog SSE messages merely refresh snapshots. Reloading or navigating away discards all entries, and changes from another browser or the CLI never appear.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or delete a runtime model, navigate away and return to Setup. Catalog history is empty despite the recent change. A change made in another client is also absent.

findings.title: A failed routing load leaves the retry picker permanently loading
findings.detail: The rejection handler sets the error but never clears loading or provides a way to retry the fetch. The picker stays hidden and submission stays disabled even after connectivity recovers. Executing the extracted mount callback with a rejected getRouting returned {"loading":true,"error":"Error: temporary outage","retryDisabled":true}. Recovery requires closing and reopening the panel.
findings.failure_scenario: Open Retry with different models for a run without model overrides while GET /api/routing temporarily fails. Restoring connectivity does not make the open picker usable.

findings.title: Clearing default effort preserves the old value
findings.detail: An empty default-effort field omits effort from the PATCH payload. RuntimeCatalog.patch merges the payload over the existing model, so the old effort survives. Isolated execution of the submit handler confirmed patchHasEffort=false and mergedEffort="high" after clearing the field. Removing that effort from supportedEfforts simultaneously also makes the API reject the otherwise valid edit.
findings.failure_scenario: Edit a runtime model with effort="high", clear Default effort, and save. The model still defaults to high. If Supported efforts is also cleared, saving fails with model.effort: absent from efforts.

findings.title: Catalog history disappears whenever Setup unmounts
findings.detail: Catalog history comes exclusively from the component-local session signal, populated by this component's mutation callbacks. Navigating away or reloading discards every entry, and catalog changes made through another client never appear. This does not provide the requested recent catalog-change history despite live catalog refreshes.
findings.failure_scenario: Add, edit or delete a runtime model, navigate to Models, then return to Setup. Catalog history is empty even though the change remains persisted.

gold.summary: Digest actions are derived from stale records instead of current unanswered and review state.
A historical failed review hides a later approval in MCP status.

findings.title: Answered questions remain in the needs-you digest
findings.detail: The digest reconstructs current attention state exclusively from feed events, but answering a question and resuming execution emit none of its clearing events. An inline `bun -` reproduction using an in-memory Store printed `current status: running open questions: 0`, followed by `Needs you: 1; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0` and the already answered question. Every subsequent session continues requesting attention until the run reaches a clearing status.
findings.failure_scenario: A run asks a question, the user answers it without acknowledging the feed, and execution resumes. Starting a new session while it runs reports the answered question as needing attention.

findings.title: A historical failed round overrides a subsequent valid approval
findings.detail: The latest round's failure is returned before examining the current approval. The existing review API allows approving the current head after a failed or cancelled round, so that round does not necessarily describe the next action. An inline `bun -` reproduction supplied a succeeded parent, OPEN PR, matching non-stale approval, and failed round; explainStatus returned `Review changes failed` with `Inspect review round round1 with limitless_get_run before submitting another verdict.` It should report that the approved PR can be queued for landing.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round fails, its findings are addressed manually, and the reviewer successfully approves the resulting head. limitless_status still tells the next agent to investigate the old failure and submit another verdict.

findings.title: Externally merged PRs retain blocked-land alerts
findings.detail: Blocked lands are cleared only by another queue request or a queue-confirmed landing. A GitHub-confirmed external merge or closure does not remove them. An inline `bun -` reproduction passed land.blocked followed by pr.merged for the same URL; output remained `Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 1`. This leaves obsolete actionable rows in the bounded session digest.
findings.failure_scenario: A land attempt blocks, a maintainer merges the PR outside the queue, and the poller records the merge. The next session still reports that landing as blocked.

findings.title: PRs remain awaiting review while requested changes are running
findings.detail: review.round_started is ignored, leaving the original run.pr_opened or previous review.round_delivered item marked as awaiting review throughout implementation of the requested changes. An inline `bun -` reproduction supplied run.pr_opened followed by review.round_started for the same PR; output was `Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0`. The existing review API refuses another changes verdict while a round remains active.
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer requests changes and the factory starts a review round. A fresh session is told to review the old head again while those changes are still being implemented.

findings.title: Recognize the run's confirmed merged flag
findings.detail: resolveMergedRun preserves status=succeeded and resolution=null while setting merged=true. The new schema discards merged, so status misses a confirmed merge when no PR snapshot or landed entry exists. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-boundaries.ts". Output: "actual state: PR state unknown merged: true" followed by "FAIL confirmed merge without poller snapshot".
findings.failure_scenario: A successful run's PR is merged outside the land queue and reconciled while GitHub polling is disabled. limitless_status reports unknown PR state instead of Landed.

findings.title: Let a subsequent approval supersede a failed review round
findings.detail: A failed or cancelled historical round takes precedence over the current valid approval indefinitely. The existing review API permits approving the current head after such a round. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-boundaries.ts". Output: "actual state: Review changes failed" followed by "FAIL new approval supersedes a failed review round"; expected "Approved; landing not queued".
findings.failure_scenario: A review round fails, a human fixes or accepts the current PR head, and limitless_review approves it. limitless_status continues directing the agent to inspect the failed round instead of offering landing.

findings.title: Clear blocked lands when their PR merges or closes
findings.detail: Blocked-land candidates are cleared only by queue events, so merging the PR externally leaves a stale actionable blocker. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-boundaries.ts". Output: "actual counts: Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 1" followed by "FAIL blocked land cleared by confirmed merge"; expected Blocked lands: 0.
findings.failure_scenario: A land blocks on CI, then an operator merges the PR externally. Both land.blocked and run.merged remain unread, and every digest still advertises the completed PR as blocked.

findings.title: Remove review requests while a review round is underway
findings.detail: review.round_started does not clear the original run.pr_opened candidate. The digest therefore advertises another review while the requested changes are already being applied. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-boundaries.ts". Output: "actual counts: Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0" followed by "FAIL review request no longer pending while round runs".
findings.failure_scenario: A PR opens and receives a changes verdict that creates a queued or running review round before the consumer acknowledges the feed. The next digest still lists the original head as awaiting review.

findings.title: Exclude questions that have already been answered
findings.detail: Answering a question and resuming execution produces none of the listed clearing events. Folding unread feed items alone keeps the answered question in Needs you until the run terminates. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-boundaries.ts". Output: "actual counts: Needs you: 1; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0" followed by "FAIL answered question no longer needs input".
findings.failure_scenario: An operator answers a waiting run through the UI or another consumer without advancing this consumer's cursor. The run resumes, but the session digest still asks for input that has already been supplied.

findings.title: Unread PR events can hide a newly required review
findings.detail: Only three event kinds seed review candidates. After the consumer acknowledges the original PR and approval events, a new head with a stale approval is ignored when its unread event is pr.ci_passed, pr.ci_failed, or another GitHub event. Current-state reconciliation never runs for that PR. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-boundaries.ts" new-head. Output: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0" despite the changed head requiring review.
findings.failure_scenario: A consumer acknowledges an approved PR, another commit changes its head, and CI passes. The next session digest reports zero PRs awaiting review.

findings.title: Exclude active review rounds from PRs awaiting review
findings.detail: The review eligibility predicate ignores review.rounds. A PR whose changes verdict has started a running round remains listed as awaiting review because its approval is absent or stale. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-boundaries.ts" active-round. Output: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0" while round1 is running.
findings.failure_scenario: The original PR-opened event remains unread while a requested review round is queued or running. Every session digest incorrectly asks for another review before the revised work is delivered.

findings.title: Honor the run's confirmed merged flag
findings.detail: The status schema strips run.merged, and the landed predicate never checks it. resolveMergedRun preserves succeeded status and can record a confirmed merge without creating a PR snapshot or a merged resolution. Status then reports an unknown or reviewable PR despite confirmed delivery. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-boundaries.ts" merged-status. Output: "Confirmed merged run: PR state unknown; Inspect the PR and await a saved observation before reviewing or landing."
findings.failure_scenario: Merge reconciliation confirms an externally merged succeeded run whose saved PR snapshot is absent or stale, with no landed queue entry. limitless_status fails to report it as landed.

findings.title: Honor the run's persisted merge flag
findings.detail: The status schema strips run.merged, and the merged-state check never considers it. Existing auto-merge delivery and GitHub reconciliation persist merged=true without necessarily saving a PR snapshot or land entry. The new tool consequently reports an already merged PR as unknown or needing review. Command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-probes.test.ts"`. Probe output: Expected: "Landed"; Received: "PR state unknown".
findings.failure_scenario: A succeeded run has merged=true after automatic delivery, prSnapshot=null, no merged resolution, and no land entry. limitless_status instructs the agent to await an observation instead of reporting completion.

findings.title: Consider new PR events when discovering pending reviews
findings.detail: Only PR-opened, round-delivered and approval events seed the review candidates. After those events are acknowledged, subsequent CI or comment events never cause the current review state to be inspected. A changed head with a stale approval is therefore silently omitted. Command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-probes.test.ts"`. Probe output: Expected: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0"; Received: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0".
findings.failure_scenario: The consumer acknowledges a PR's opening and approval. Someone pushes another commit, invalidating the approval, and polling emits pr.ci_passed for that head. The next session digest reports zero PRs awaiting review.

findings.title: Exclude active changes rounds from reviews awaiting action

findings.failure_scenario: A PR is opened, the reviewer requests changes without acknowledging its opening event, and the factory queues a review round. SessionStart continues presenting the original head as awaiting review.

findings.title: Do not redact executable configuration when restoring state
findings.detail: redactGateData rewrites every string in RunState, including gatesConfig check commands and baselineScripts. Consequently, restarting a run can change the checks it executes. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {registerCredential,sh} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import {redactGateData} from "./src/gates/output.ts"; const secret="synthetic-config-token-421"; registerCredential("REVIEW_TOKEN",secret); const state={gatesConfig:{checks:[{name:"fixture",run:`test "$FIXTURE_TOKEN" = "${secret}"`}]}}; const resumed=redactGateData(state); const results=[]; for (const s of [state,resumed]) {const r=await sh(["/bin/sh","-c",s.gatesConfig.checks[0].run],{cwd:process.cwd(),env:{FIXTURE_TOKEN:secret},allo
findings.failure_scenario: A persisted gate command contains a registered credential literal. Before restart it runs as configured; after restart the literal becomes [redacted], changing the command and its result.

findings.title: Bound the carry buffer for self-overlapping credentials
findings.detail: Overlapping matches can repeatedly move cut backward to zero, retaining the entire raw stream instead of a bounded credential prefix. Each retreat also searches the growing suffix for absent variants, causing quadratic work and blocking the parent's event loop and timeout handling. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {runProcess,registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; registerCredential("REVIEW_TOKEN","abcde\nabcde\n"); const start=performance.now(); await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e",`process.stdout.write("abcde\\n".repeat(200000))`],cwd:process.cwd(),env:{},redactOutput:true}); console.log(JSON.stringify({bytes:1200000,elapsedMs:Math.round(performance.now()-start)}));' Ou
findings.failure_scenario: Register a credential such as abcde\nabcde\n and have a gate continuously print abcde followed by a newline. The carry grows with total output, repeated scans consume the daemon's event loop, and gate timeout callbacks cannot run promptly.

findings.title: Redaction can destroy the sandbox startup token
findings.detail: Enabling runner redaction also redacts the trusted `limitless-started-<uuid>` line before runSandboxed compares it with its token. Registering the valid eight-character credential `limitless` makes a successfully executed command throw ConfinementError. Reproduced with: bun -e 'import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import {runSandboxed} from "./src/harness/sandbox.ts"; registerCredential("TEST_PASSWORD","limitless"); try {await runSandboxed({cmd:["/usr/bin/true"],cwd:process.cwd(),env:{},redactOutput:true},{write:[],protect:[]},undefined,async()=>{},{verify:async()=>{},wrap:cmd=>cmd}); console.log("PASS");} catch(e) {console.log(e.constructor.name+": "+e.message);}' Output:
findings.failure_scenario: A registered credential matches a fixed substring of the startup token, such as `limitless`. Every gate then reports a confinement startup failure even though its payload started and exited successfully.
